newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cue seeks PNG exploration licences.
newsitem.headline: Cue seeks PNG exploration licences.

text.p: Cue Energy Resources No Liability said on Wednesday it had applied with its joint venture partners for two new petroleum prospecting licences (PPLs) in Papua New Guinea over the area of the current PPL 56 which expires in December.

Cue also said the government of Papua New Guinea had given formal notice it would exercise its right to take up a 22.5 percent interest in the Development Licence Area relating to the PPL 56 portion of the SE Gobe oilfield.

The first PPL application is in the northern 22 block covering the "highly oil prospective fold belt portion" of PPL 56. A new licence would enable a vigorous oil exploration programme for a further 11 years.

Cue will increase its equity from seven percent in PPL 56 to 10.535 percent in the northern licence area, where the other partners are Barracuda Pty Ltd (30.1 percent), Iona Pty Ltd (30.1 percent), Mountain West Exploration Inc (3.76 percent) and Southern Highlands Petroleum Co (25.5 percent).

The second application is in the southern 23 block area which covers the foreland portion of PPL 56 and contains the Barikewa gas field. The joint venture intends to pursue the commercialisation of Barikewa and further explore the hydrocarbon potential of the area.
Cue will increase its equity from seven percent to 14.1 percent in the southern area, where the other partners are Barracuda Pty (40.4 percent), Iona (40.4 percent) and Mountain West (5.01 percent).
Cue said the PNG government, in exercising its right to a 22.5 stake of the PPL 56 portion of SE Gobe, would reimburse past costs, plus interest, associated with the stake.
It said this would be a significant addition to Cue's working capital.
The SE Gobe Field is being developed by Chevron Nigini Pty Limited under a unitisation agreement. First oil production is expected in late 1997.
